summary: Focused re-review of the three prior blockers approves the exact verified revision. Due scheduled cadence is retained as inert internal state and is failed without creating provider outbox work; dispatchable outbox rows must carry operator_control provenance, match their stable communication identity, and resolve to the persisted communication.queued event before the network boundary. Public PostgreSQL URLs now reject disable, allow, prefer, missing, duplicate, and unknown sslmode values while accepting Railway-private/local connections and require/verify-ca/verify-full. CRON_SECRET now fails closed unless it contains at least 32 bytes and at least 128 estimated entropy bits. The independent remediation suite passed 3/3, and verification-report.json records PASSED evidence for implementation commit 7b1fc2aa8c7c2225fd3be032581c4a2521f3ef72. No unresolved blocking security finding remains.

findings.description: Resolved: runTick never materializes scheduled cadence into outbox work and rejects unauthorized or forged legacy rows before provider dispatch. Authorized rows require operator_control, communication_id equal to stable_action_id, and a matching persisted communication.queued event for the same event, scenario, aggregate, and channel.
findings.impact: Reset-seeded schedules and public database-local commands cannot cross the provider boundary; only the operator-authenticated communication path creates dispatchable work.
findings.remediation: None required for this task; retain the focused scheduler authorization regression tests.

findings.description: Resolved: non-local, non-Railway-private PostgreSQL URLs must declare exactly one sslmode in require, verify-ca, or verify-full; disable, allow, prefer, missing, duplicate, and unknown modes fail closed.
findings.impact: The runtime no longer accepts a public database URL that explicitly disables or weakens TLS.
findings.remediation: None required for this task; keep Railway PostgreSQL private as documented.

findings.description: Resolved: runtime and manual-tick preflight require CRON_SECRET to contain at least 32 bytes and at least 128 estimated entropy bits before constant-time bearer comparison.
findings.impact: Short, empty, repetitive, or accidentally truncated scheduler credentials cannot authenticate or leave runtime health appearing ready.
findings.remediation: None required for this task; generate and store the secret through Railway's sealed server variables.
